methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: AI Ready Roanoke represents a deliberate regional capacity-building effort outside traditional tech hubs, suggesting distributed AI fluency is achievable through intentional community organizing rather than waiting for platform solutions or metro spillover.

signals.title: AI is already common in Virginia Beach high schools. Leaders weigh guardrails - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Widespread AI adoption in Virginia Beach high schools with policy discussions around guardrails indicates platform-driven shallow distribution—students use AI tools ubiquitously but the focus on safety rather than deep capability development reveals superficial engagement.

signals.title: UVA President Scott Beardsley charts University’s future in artificial intelligence - UVA Today
signals.signal_reading: UVA's presidential focus on AI strategy concentrates institutional resources and elite talent development in Charlottesville, reinforcing the research-university-to-innovation-hub pipeline that deepens capability in metro-adjacent academic centers while other regions lack equivalent infrastructure.

signals.title: News Flash Archive - NPD E911 Division implements Artificial Intelligence (AI) system on non-emergency lines - City of Norfolk (.gov)
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk's deployment of AI for 911 non-emergency call routing represents municipal adoption of turnkey platform solutions—distributed geographically but shallow in local capability development, as the city consumes rather than develops AI capacity.

signals.title: Rural advocacy groups band together to oppose data centers, related energy projects
signals.signal_reading: Rural coalitions organizing against data centers signal communities experiencing AI infrastructure as extractive burden rather than capacity-building opportunity, suggesting neither depth nor distribution is materializing in non-metro regions despite proximity to physical AI infrastructure.
